t: This is Oliver Goldsmith Primary School, in Southwark, named after the Anglo-Irish writer Oliver Goldsmith. He was a poet, novelist and playwright, and is considered one of the most versatile writers of the Georgian era. His best-known works include his only novel, The Vicar of Wakefield, from 1766, and the comedy She Stoops to Conquer, from 1773. The comedies are ranked second in importance on the English stage only to Shakespeare's. The school carries his name as a tribute to his place in English literature.
